summary: This Dockerfile creates a web server image based on Apache HTTP Server 2.4, installs necessary tools and PHP support, configures SSL certificates for secure connections, and enables the required Apache modules to run a custom site configuration with SSL and URL rewriting capabilities.

explanations.2: This starts with a pre-built image that already has Apache 2.4 installed, so we don't have to set everything up from scratch.
explanations.6: The backslash at the end of the line tells Docker to continue this command on the next line, making a long command more readable.
explanations.8: This installs three packages: apache2-utils (tools for Apache), libapache2-mod-php (allows Apache to run PHP code), and openssl (for secure connections). The --no-install-recommends flag skips extra packages we don't strictly need.
explanations.10: After installing packages, we delete the package cache files to make the image smaller.
explanations.14: We copy an SSL certificate file from our computer into the container so Apache can use it for secure HTTPS connections.
explanations.16: We copy the private key that goes with the certificate—this is secret and proves the server is authentic.
explanations.23: The sed command finds and uncomments specific lines in Apache's main configuration file by removing the # symbol at the start of those lines.
explanations.25: This uncomment step enables Apache to load and use SSL (secure connection) configuration.
explanations.27: This uncomment step loads the mod_ssl module, which is Apache's extension for handling HTTPS.
explanations.29: This uncomment step loads a memory caching module that SSL uses to improve performance.
explanations.35: a2enmod means 'Apache 2 enable module'—we're turning on the ssl module so Apache can use it.
explanations.37: We enable the rewrite module, which lets Apache redirect or rewrite URLs based on rules.
explanations.39: a2dissite means 'Apache 2 disable site'—we're turning off the default Apache sites so only our custom site runs.
explanations.41: We enable our custom my-site configuration so Apache will actually serve it.
